questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.**

The recent lawsuit _____ put the firm in a tight spot.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'has'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **In the given blank,** *we need a singular verb because the subject of the sentence is singular in number i.e. 'lawsuit' also after the blank the irregular form of the verb has been written and this verb should be in the third form of the verb so we need a helping which is going to be 'has'*

**So the correct sentence is-** *The recent lawsuit **has** put the firm in a tight spot.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.**

Tourism has been _____ in India for a long time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Neglected'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Let's see the meaning of the given words-

 
• **Neglected:** Refers to the act of being ignored or being out of focus
 
• **Postponed-** arrange for (something) to take place at a time later than that first scheduled.
 
• **Declined-** politely refuse.
 
• **Decayed-** decline in quality or vigor.

Hence, according to the meaning of the given words, the correct answer is** Option 4 i.e. 'Neglected'**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "admire."**

• **Slander**: Refers to the act of making a false statement about someone to spoil their reputation
 
• **Admire: **Refers to the act of regarding something with respect and approval

• Thus, it is clear that **slander **and **admire** are **opposite** words.
 
• Let's look at the meaning of other words:

• **Malign:** Refers to something that is evil in nature
 
• **Defame**: Refers to the act of damaging the reputation of someone
 
 

Thus, options 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Garima **__live at__ **the 25th floor.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3 i.e. 'lives on'.**

One cannot 'live in' a floor, one can only 'live on' a floor - 'live in' a flat or bungalow is correct.

Thus, options 1 and 2 are incorrect. Also, 'Garima' is a singular subject. So, *lives *should be used as the sentence is in the simple present tense.

__Correct sentence:__ *Garima __lives on__ the 25th floor.*

questions.solution:

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Rakesh was studied when his friends called him.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'studied when'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

In this part of the sentence, the usage of **'studied when'** is incorrect Instead, use '**studying when**' 

 
• The sentence is in the present continuous tense - 'studied' refers to the past tense and thus is the segment of the sentence which has a grammatical error. It should be replaced with 'studying'.

So the correct sentence is- *Rakesh **was studying** when his friends called him.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

The teacher expected the students __**had finishing**__ the project on time.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3 i.e. 'to finish'.**

Option 1 is incorrect as the verb 'expected' refers to the past tense and 'finishing' is in the present continuous tense and thus cannot be the answer. 

Option 4 is incorrect, as it is missing the preposition 'to'.

Thus, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

V**irat Kohli is one of the best batsmen that the world have seen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3. 

'The world' is a singular entity and thus it has to be referred to in a singular term. 'Have' is used for a plural entity and so this needs to be replaced with 'has'.

Thus, the correct sentence is : *Virat Kohli is one of the best batsmen that the world **has** seen.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Shashi couldn't walk __**no more**__.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2 i.e. any farther.**

Option 1 is incorrect as 'farther' is already a comparative term, thus the 'more' is unnecessary.

Option 3 is incorrect because 'more' is a comparative term that needs to be used before the adverb 'far'.

Thus, the correct answer is option 2.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.**

In the age of technology, sending letters by postal mail seems __________ to me.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4 i.e. 'superfluous'.**

'Superfluous' Refers to something that is unnecessary.

The sentence means that in the times of technology, sending messages by post is unnecessary.

Let's look at the meaning of other words:

 
• **Superstition:** Refers to a belief that is respectful of the supernatural
 
• **Surplus:** Refers to something that is more than what is needed, something that is in excess
 
• **Supercilious:** Refers to someone who thinks or looks as though they are superior to others. 

 

Thus, the correct answer is option 4.
